page: Amazon Web Services x1e.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Xen hypervisor, designed for workloads requiring substantial volatile memory capacity. Powered by an Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz, the system exposes 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It is equipped with 976.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 30.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware features include 45 MB of shared L3 cache, standard AVX support, AES cryptography, and BMI2 instructions, though newer instruction sets like AVX-512 are not present.

Local physical storage consists of a dedicated 960 GB solid-state drive, complementing its primary compute profile. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 5 Gbps. The instance operates without discrete GPU acceleration. In terms of compute performance, the older Broadwell-era architecture shows its limitations in single-threaded tasks, placing in the bottom tier on Geekbench single-core (843.0) and stress-ng single-core (722.29). Multi-core throughput remains in the middle tier, producing a PassMark CPU score of 18,782.43 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 7,244.0.

Memory throughput reaches 63.28 GB/sec for large-block uncached reads and 30.54 GB/sec for writes. In application-focused tests, the instance delivered 18.29 million Redis SET operations per second and handled PassMark database operations at an average performance level. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the platform trades off per-core compute efficiency and single-thread velocity to deliver exceptionally high memory density per instance. Consequently, this server is suitable for large in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive key-value caches, and memory-bound enterprise data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services x1e.8xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine tailored for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Driven by an Intel Xeon E7-8880 v3 processor running at 2.3 GHz, it delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores) and an extensive 976.0 GB memory footprint, translating to roughly 30.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. The hardware profile includes a 960 GB local SSD and 5 Gbps baseline networking, without GPU acceleration. Benchmark profiles indicate modest single-thread capabilities, scoring in the lower tier for single-core tasks, while multi-core workloads, memory bandwidth, and Redis SET operations demonstrate middle-tier results. This hardware allocation represents a targeted trade-off, prioritizing massive RAM capacity over modern core efficiency. The system is suited for in-memory databases, large caching layers, and high-footprint enterprise batch processing.
